QPR players and fans are feeling confident before their important match against Aston Villa this Tuesday. 

Before their big 4-1 win against West Brom last Saturday, QPR had lost 13 of their last 14 away games. That win ended a five-game losing streak. QPR is currently in 19th place, only three points away from avoiding relegation.

During the win, coach Chris Ramsey told his players to stay calm. He also said, "It' is a great win for us. The team's mood has been good and everyone has acted very professionally."

This kept a special streak alive: in all 187 professional rounds she has played, she has made at least one birdie every single time.

Arsene Wenger hasn't decided if he will give Abou Diaby a new contract yet. However, he suggested that the midfielder might stay at Arsenal after this summer. Diaby has struggled with injuries, playing only 22 games in the last five seasons because he spent much of his time recovering. He returned to play in a practice game this Wednesday. Arsenal plays Liverpool this Saturday, but Wenger likely won't make Diaby play in such an important game right away. He did suggest that Diaby could earn a new contract, possibly one where he only gets paid when he actually plays.

Even without stars like Tiger Woods or Rory McIlroy, the Shell Houston Open in Humble is seeing record-breaking crowds. Because it is the last tournament before the Masters, it is a huge success. This is largely due to the excitement caused by Phil Mickelson and local favorite Jordan Spieth. 

Just 18 months ago, Spieth was criticized for leaving university to join the PGA Tour as a low-ranked player. Now, at only 21 years old, he is ranked number four in the world. Interestingly, no one is criticizing him anymore.
